chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"It is not valid for a man to sell using a sa' that is not the sa' of Misr."

key_terms.صَاعٍ: A traditional unit of volume measure used for dry goods
key_terms.صَاعِ اَلْمِصْرِ: The standard measure of Egypt, used as a reference for validity

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using a non-standard measure for selling goods in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on standardizing commercial measures to prevent *gharar* (uncertainty) and ensure equity in trade. By specifying the 'Sa' of Misr, it highlights the historical reliance on widely accepted regional standards to maintain trust in market transactions. This ruling reflects the broader Islamic principle of preserving economic justice through precise and transparent measurement.
